# 单篇讲义生成任务

项目仓库: vllm-project/semantic-router
项目名: semantic-router
讲义目录: semantic-router-tutorial/
代码永久链接 base: https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/blob/7a77e1e1b1d5711d0b94e3c75bcea694a1d1f246/
当前 HEAD: 7a77e1e1b1d5711d0b94e3c75bcea694a1d1f246
动作: new


---

## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论）

# 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你不能：

- 修改源码
- 写入任何 `.md` 文件
- 输出 JSON 以外的文字

你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。

---

## 总目标

为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。

这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。

每篇讲义应该满足：

1. 面向初学者也能读懂。
2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。
3. 必须结合真实源码。
4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。

---

## 源码探查顺序

请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节：

1. 项目说明
   - README
   - docs
   - examples
   - tutorials

2. 构建与运行方式
   - package.json
   - Cargo.toml
   - pyproject.toml
   - go.mod
   - pom.xml
   - Makefile
   - Dockerfile
   - CI 配置

3. 项目入口
   - CLI 入口
   - Web 服务入口
   - main 文件
   - library export 文件
   - examples 入口

4. 目录结构
   - src
   - lib
   - app
   - packages
   - crates
   - tests

5. 核心流程
   - 初始化流程
   - 配置加载
   - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路
   - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制

6. 测试与示例
   - 单元测试
   - 集成测试
   - benchmark
   - example usage

---

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json
{
  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。


## 完整大纲

```json
{
  "project": "semantic-router",
  "rationale": "本项目是面向 LLM 推理的 Envoy ExtProc 控制面（Go 路由器为核心，辅以 Python CLI、推理绑定、K8s Operator、React 面板、E2E 与仿真），体量大、跨语言，因此采用「先全局后内核、先概念后源码」的三层路径。入门层（U1–U3）先让读者建立 Mixture-of-Models + 信号-投影-决策的心智模型，再掌握 vllm-sr CLI 的运行方式与 v0.3 配置/Recipe 体系，建立可直接跑起来的能力。进阶层（U4–U9）沿着真实请求主链路 Envoy→ExtProc→分类信号→投影→决策→选择→后端 展开，并深入向量检索、语义缓存与记忆等运行时子系统，同时讲解可把 YAML 与 DSL 互转的路由 DSL。专家层（U10–U14）覆盖插件链、控制面 API、可观测性、多后端适配、Operator/CRD 与推理绑定、面板、E2E 与仿真、训练评估等扩展与工程化主题。单元之间遵循「概念→配置→启动→请求链路→决策选择→DSL→信号→存储缓存→插件→控制面→部署→面板→测试」的依赖顺序，每篇讲义只解决一个独立主题、引用 1–6 个真实源码文件并给出可操作的实践任务。",

    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "项目入门与定位",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [

          "id": "u1-l1",

          "topic": "介绍 vLLM Semantic Router 作为面向 LLM 推理的可编程路由层，解释 Mixture-of-Models、信号驱动路由与 Envoy ExtProc 控制面的定位与价值。",
          "learning_goals": [

            "了解项目的核心研究问题（信号捕获、信号组合、模型协作、Token 经济、安全可观测）"

        },

          "learning_goals": [
            "掌握 src/semantic-router、src/vllm-sr、config、deploy、dashboard、e2e、tools 等目录的职责",
            "理解仓库没有根 docs/scripts catch-all 的边界约定",
```

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 项目概览与定位：什么是 vLLM Semantic Router

本讲是整本学习手册的概念底座，覆盖三个最小模块。项目定位：vLLM SR（vLLM Semantic Router）是面向异构 LLM 基础设施的可编程路由层，位于客户端与模型后端之间，在不把路由逻辑硬编码进应用的前提下，同时改善质量（quality）、成本（cost）、延迟（latency）、隐私（privacy）、安全（safety）五个维度。核心理念：Mixture-of-Models（MoM，混合模型）——承认「最好的模型是一个组合」，通过 Signals（信号，项目维护 16 个信号族）→ Projections（投影，将相互竞争的信号协调为命名路由带）→ Decisions（决策，用 AND/OR 布尔规则求值）三层，把信号变成可执行的路由。工程形态：以 Envoy External Processor（ext_proc）控制面落地，Envoy 负责搬流量、SR 负责做智能决策，使路由成为可观察、可配置的基础设施层。引入的关键术语包括 routing、signal、control plane、entrypoint、recipe、backend、plugin；其一句话执行流程为 entrypoint → recipe（signals + projections + decisions）→ select backend(s) → apply plugins，这正是后续请求处理主链路讲义的骨架。项目由 5 个核心研究问题驱动演进；仓库为多语言 monorepo（Go 路由内核位于 `src/semantic-router/`、Python CLI/编排位于 `src/vllm-sr/`），唯一公开文档树为 `website/`。
### u1-l2 仓库结构与目录组织

本讲承接 u1-l1 的路由概念，从工程师视角梳理 vLLM Semantic Router 多语言 monorepo 的目录组织，覆盖三个最小模块。第一，资产边界：顶层目录按归属和生命周期划分所有权，`config/` 拥有配置与 recipe，`deploy/` 拥有部署产物，`website/` 是唯一公开文档树；仓库故意没有根 `docs/`、`scripts/` 兜底目录，根文件受 `tools/agent/structure-rules.yaml` 的可执行白名单约束。第二，核心子系统映射：路由内核 `src/semantic-router/`(Go) 执行决策，`src/vllm-sr/`(Python) 做本地编排，各 `*-binding/`(Rust) 提供推理能力，并主动抽取 `pkg/milvus/` 等共享层。第三，入口定位：本地服务从 `src/vllm-sr/cli/main.py` 进入，Go 路由器从 `cmd/main.go` 进入。最后须区分目录级的 High-Risk Areas 与文件级的 Known Hotspots，改动热点遵循「抽取优先」。

```json
  "rationale": "本项目是面向 LLM 推理的 Envoy ExtProc 控制面（Go 路由器为核心，辅以 Python CLI、推理绑定、K8s Operator、React 面板、E2E 与仿真），体量大、跨语言，因此采用「先全局后内核、先概念后源码」的三层路径。入门层（U1–U3）先让读者建立 Mixture-of-Models + 信号-投影-决策的心智模型，再掌握 vllm-sr CLI 的运行方式与 v0.3 配置/Recipe 体系，建立可直接跑起来的能力。进阶层（U4–U9）沿着真实请求主链路 Envoy→ExtProc→分类信号→投影→决策→选择→后端 展开，并深入向量检索、语义缓存与记忆等运行时子系统，同时讲解可把 YAML 与 DSL 互转的路由 DSL。专家层（U10–U14）覆盖插件链、控制面 API、可观测性、多后端适配、Operator/CRD 与推理绑定、面板、E2E 与仿真、训练评估等扩展与工程化主题。单元之间遵循「概念→配置→启动→请求链路→决策选择→DSL→信号→存储缓存→插件→控制面→部署→面板→测试」的依赖顺序，每篇讲义只解决一个独立主题、引用 1–6 个真实源码文件并给出可操作的实践任务。",
```

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 项目概览与定位：什么是 vLLM Semantic Router

本讲是整本学习手册的概念底座，覆盖三个最小模块。项目定位：vLLM SR（vLLM Semantic Router）是面向异构 LLM 基础设施的可编程路由层，位于客户端与模型后端之间，在不把路由逻辑硬编码进应用的前提下，同时改善质量（quality）、成本（cost）、延迟（latency）、隐私（privacy）、安全（safety）五个维度。核心理念：Mixture-of-Models（MoM，混合模型）——承认「最好的模型是一个组合」，通过 Signals（信号，项目维护 16 个信号族）→ Projections（投影，将相互竞争的信号协调为命名路由带）→ Decisions（决策，用 AND/OR 布尔规则求值）三层，把信号变成可执行的路由。工程形态：以 Envoy External Processor（ext_proc）控制面落地，Envoy 负责搬流量、SR 负责做智能决策，使路由成为可观察、可配置的基础设施层。引入的关键术语包括 routing、signal、control plane、entrypoint、recipe、backend、plugin；其一句话执行流程为 entrypoint → recipe（signals + projections + decisions）→ select backend(s) → apply plugins，这正是后续请求处理主链路讲义的骨架。项目由 5 个核心研究问题驱动演进；仓库为多语言 monorepo（Go 路由内核位于 `src/semantic-router/`、Python CLI/编排位于 `src/vllm-sr/`），唯一公开文档树为 `website/`。
### u1-l2 仓库结构与目录组织

本讲承接 u1-l1 的路由概念，从工程师视角梳理 vLLM Semantic Router 多语言 monorepo 的目录组织，覆盖三个最小模块。第一，资产边界：顶层目录按归属和生命周期划分所有权，`config/` 拥有配置与 recipe，`deploy/` 拥有部署产物，`website/` 是唯一公开文档树；仓库故意没有根 `docs/`、`scripts/` 兜底目录，根文件受 `tools/agent/structure-rules.yaml` 的可执行白名单约束。第二，核心子系统映射：路由内核 `src/semantic-router/`(Go) 执行决策，`src/vllm-sr/`(Python) 做本地编排，各 `*-binding/`(Rust) 提供推理能力，并主动抽取 `pkg/milvus/` 等共享层。第三，入口定位：本地服务从 `src/vllm-sr/cli/main.py` 进入，Go 路由器从 `cmd/main.go` 进入。最后须区分目录级的 High-Risk Areas 与文件级的 Known Hotspots，改动热点遵循「抽取优先」。

923	      --runtime)

931	        shift 2

935	        BIN_DIR="$2"
936	        shift 2
937	        ;;
938	      --pip-spec)

940	        PIP_SPEC="$2"
941	        shift 2
942	        ;;
943	      --channel)
944	        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --channel"
945	        REQUESTED_CHANNEL="$2"
946	        shift 2
947	        ;;

955	        REQUESTED_PLATFORM="$2"

961	        ;;
962	      -h|--help)

964	        exit 0
965	        ;;

968	        ;;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

MODE="${VLLM_SR_INSTALL_MODE:-serve}"
REQUESTED_RUNTIME="${VLLM_SR_RUNTIME:-auto}"
INSTALL_ROOT="${VLLM_SR_INSTALL_ROOT:-$HOME/.local/share/vllm-sr}"
BIN_DIR="${VLLM_SR_BIN_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
PIP_SPEC="${VLLM_SR_PIP_SPEC:-}"
REQUESTED_CHANNEL="${VLLM_SR_INSTALL_CHANNEL:-dev}"
PYTHON_BIN="${VLLM_SR_PYTHON:-}"
REQUESTED_PLATFORM="${VLLM_SR_INSTALL_PLATFORM:-${VLLM_SR_PLATFORM:-auto}}"
AUTO_LAUNCH="${VLLM_SR_INSTALL_AUTO_LAUNCH:-1}"

OS_NAME=""
SELECTED_RUNTIME=""
LAUNCH_PLATFORM=""
AUTO_LAUNCH_RAN="0"
STYLE_BOLD=""
COLOR_RESET=""
COLOR_ORANGE=""
COLOR_BLUE=""
COLOR_WHITE=""
COLOR_MUTED=""
COLOR_SUCCESS=""

DASHBOARD_URL="http://localhost:8700"

init_colors() {
  if [ ! -t 1 ] || [ -n "${NO_COLOR:-}" ]; then
    return
  fi

  STYLE_BOLD=$'\033[1m'
  COLOR_RESET=$'\033[0m'
  COLOR_ORANGE=$'\033[38;2;254;181;22m'
  COLOR_BLUE=$'\033[38;2;48;162;255m'
  COLOR_WHITE=$'\033[97m'
  COLOR_MUTED=$'\033[38;2;145;158;171m'
  COLOR_SUCCESS=$'\033[38;2;111;224;161m'
}

print_logo() {
  if [ "${VLLM_SR_NO_LOGO:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    return
  fi

  init_colors

  printf '\n'
  printf '%b\n' "  ${STYLE_BOLD}${COLOR_WHITE}       █     █     █▄   ▄█${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '%b\n' "  ${STYLE_BOLD}${COLOR_WHITE} ▄▄ ▄█ █     █     █ ▀▄▀ █${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '%b\n' "  ${STYLE_BOLD}${COLOR_WHITE}  █▄█▀ █     █     █     █${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '%b\n' "  ${STYLE_BOLD}${COLOR_WHITE}   ▀▀  ▀▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀▀ ▀     ▀${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '%b\n' "  ${STYLE_BOLD}${COLOR_WHITE}  Semantic Router${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '%b\n' "  ${COLOR_MUTED}  local installer${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '\n'
}

step() {
  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_BLUE}[step]${COLOR_RESET} $*"
}

done_step() {
  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_SUCCESS}[done]${COLOR_RESET} $*"
}

info() {
  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_MUTED}[info]${COLOR_RESET} $*"
}

warn() {
  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_ORANGE}[warn]${COLOR_RESET} $*" >&2
}

die() {
  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_ORANGE}[error]${COLOR_RESET} $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

is_truthy() {
  case "${1:-}" in
    1|true|TRUE|yes|YES|on|ON)
      return 0
      ;;
    *)
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

is_falsey() {
  case "${1:-}" in
    0|false|FALSE|no|NO|off|OFF)
      return 0
      ;;
    *)
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

auto_launch_enabled() {
  is_truthy "$AUTO_LAUNCH"
}

should_auto_launch() {
  auto_launch_enabled || return 1
  [ "$MODE" = "serve" ] || return 1
  [ "$REQUESTED_RUNTIME" != "skip" ] || return 1
}

describe_package_channel() {
  if [ -n "$PIP_SPEC" ]; then
    printf 'custom (--pip-spec override)\n'
    return
  fi

  printf '%s\n' "$REQUESTED_CHANNEL"
}

describe_package_selection() {
  if [ -n "$PIP_SPEC" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$PIP_SPEC"
    return
  fi

  case "$REQUESTED_CHANNEL" in
    dev)
      printf 'vllm-sr (--pre, latest development release)\n'
      ;;
    stable)
      printf 'vllm-sr (latest stable release)\n'
      ;;
  esac
}

print_install_plan() {
  local requested_runtime python_cmd python_version runtime_cmd package_manager
  requested_runtime="$REQUESTED_RUNTIME"
  if [ "$REQUESTED_RUNTIME" = "auto" ]; then
    case "$OS_NAME" in
      darwin)
        requested_runtime="auto -> docker/colima"
        ;;
      linux)
        requested_runtime="auto -> docker"
        ;;
    esac
  fi

  python_cmd="$(detect_python_candidate || true)"
  runtime_cmd="$(detect_existing_runtime || true)"
  package_manager="$(detect_package_manager_label)"

  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_WHITE}Detected environment${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '  platform     %s (%s)\n' "$(detect_os_label)" "$(uname -m)"
  printf '  package mgr  %s\n' "$package_manager"
  if [ -n "$python_cmd" ]; then
    python_version="$(python_version_of "$python_cmd")"
    printf '  python       %s (%s)\n' "$python_cmd" "$python_version"
  else
    printf '  python       not found (needs Python 3.10+)\n'
  fi
  if [ -n "$runtime_cmd" ]; then
    printf '  runtime      %s (ready)\n' "$runtime_cmd"
  else
    printf '  runtime      none detected\n'
  fi
  printf '\n'

  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_WHITE}Install plan${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '  mode         %s\n' "$MODE"
  printf '  runtime      %s\n' "$requested_runtime"
  printf '  launch       %s\n' "$(if should_auto_launch; then printf 'auto first-run'; else printf 'manual'; fi)"
  printf '  platform     %s\n' "$(display_platform_plan)"
  printf '  channel      %s\n' "$(describe_package_channel)"
  printf '  python deps  pip, setuptools, wheel\n'
  printf '  package      %s\n' "$(describe_package_selection)"
  printf '  system deps  %s\n' "$(describe_python_dependency_plan "$python_cmd")"
  printf '  runtime deps %s\n' "$(describe_runtime_dependency_plan "$runtime_cmd")"
  printf '  install root %s\n' "$INSTALL_ROOT"
  printf '  launcher     %s/vllm-sr\n' "$BIN_DIR"
  printf '\n'
}

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: install.sh [--mode cli|serve] [--runtime auto|docker|skip]
                  [--install-root PATH] [--bin-dir PATH]
                  [--channel stable|dev] [--pip-spec SPEC]
                  [--python PATH] [--platform PLATFORM] [--no-launch]

Installs the vLLM Semantic Router CLI into an isolated virtual environment and
links a launcher into ~/.local/bin by default.

Options:
  --mode cli|serve         Install the CLI only, or prepare a local runtime for
                           `vllm-sr serve` as well. Default: serve
  --runtime auto|docker|skip
                           Runtime strategy for serve mode. Default: auto
                           macOS auto -> docker via colima
                           Linux auto -> docker
  --install-root PATH      Installation root. Default:
                           ~/.local/share/vllm-sr
  --bin-dir PATH           Launcher directory. Default: ~/.local/bin
  --channel stable|dev     Package channel to install when --pip-spec is not
                           set. Default: dev
  --pip-spec SPEC          Explicit Python package spec to install. Overrides
                           --channel when set
  --python PATH            Explicit Python interpreter to use
  --platform PLATFORM      Platform hint for first-run serve. Use 'amd' for ROCm.
                           Default: auto
  --no-launch              Skip the installer's automatic first `vllm-sr serve`
                           and dashboard open step
  -h, --help               Show this help message

Environment overrides:
  VLLM_SR_INSTALL_MODE
  VLLM_SR_RUNTIME
  VLLM_SR_INSTALL_ROOT
  VLLM_SR_BIN_DIR
  VLLM_SR_INSTALL_CHANNEL
  VLLM_SR_PIP_SPEC
  VLLM_SR_PYTHON
  VLLM_SR_INSTALL_PLATFORM
  VLLM_SR_INSTALL_AUTO_LAUNCH
EOF
}

has_cmd() {
  command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

make_temp_log() {
  mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vllm-sr-install.XXXXXX"
}

run_quiet_step() {
  local label log_file
  label="$1"
  shift

  step "$label"
  log_file="$(make_temp_log)"

  if "$@" >"$log_file" 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$log_file"
    done_step "$label"
    return
  fi

  warn "$label failed. Command output follows:"
  cat "$log_file" >&2
  rm -f "$log_file"
  exit 1
}

run_as_root() {
  if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
    "$@"
    return
  fi

  if has_cmd sudo; then
    sudo "$@"
    return
  fi

  die "This step requires root or sudo: $*"
}

detect_os() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin)
      OS_NAME="darwin"
      ;;
    Linux)
      OS_NAME="linux"
      ;;
    *)
      die "Unsupported operating system. This installer supports macOS and Linux."
      ;;
  esac
}

detect_os_label() {
  case "$OS_NAME" in
    darwin)
      printf 'macOS\n'
      ;;
    linux)
      printf 'Linux\n'
      ;;
    *)
      printf '%s\n' "$OS_NAME"
      ;;
  esac
}

resolve_launch_platform() {
  if [ "$REQUESTED_PLATFORM" != "auto" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$REQUESTED_PLATFORM"
    return
  fi

  if [ -n "${VLLM_SR_PLATFORM:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$VLLM_SR_PLATFORM"
    return
  fi

  if has_cmd rocm-smi || has_cmd rocminfo || [ -e /dev/kfd ] || [ -d /opt/rocm ]; then
    printf 'amd\n'
    return
  fi

  printf '\n'
}

display_platform_plan() {
  local platform
  platform="$(resolve_launch_platform)"
  if [ -n "$platform" ]; then
    if [ "$REQUESTED_PLATFORM" = "auto" ]; then
      printf '%s (auto-detected)\n' "$platform"
    else
      printf '%s\n' "$platform"
    fi
    return
  fi

  printf 'default\n'
}

detect_primary_ip() {
  local python_cmd
  python_cmd="$(detect_python_candidate || true)"
  if [ -z "$python_cmd" ]; then
    return 1
  fi

  "$python_cmd" -c '
import socket
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
try:
    s.connect(("8.8.8.8", 80))
    print(s.getsockname()[0])
finally:
    s.close()
' 2>/dev/null
}

detect_host_label() {
  hostname -f 2>/dev/null || hostname 2>/dev/null || printf 'your-server\n'
}

is_remote_session() {
  [ -n "${SSH_CONNECTION:-}" ] || [ -n "${SSH_TTY:-}" ]
}

open_dashboard_url() {
  case "$OS_NAME" in
    darwin)
      open "$DASHBOARD_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1
      ;;
    linux)
      if has_cmd xdg-open; then
        xdg-open "$DASHBOARD_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1
        return
      fi
      if has_cmd gio; then
        gio open "$DASHBOARD_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1
        return
      fi
      return 1
      ;;
    *)
      return 1
      ;;
  esac
}

print_dashboard_access() {
  local primary_ip host_label
  primary_ip="$(detect_primary_ip || true)"
  host_label="$(detect_host_label)"

  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_WHITE}Dashboard access${COLOR_RESET}"
  printf '  local        %s\n' "$DASHBOARD_URL"
  if [ -n "$primary_ip" ]; then
    printf '  network      http://%s:8700\n' "$primary_ip"
  fi
  printf '\n'

  if is_remote_session; then
    printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_WHITE}Remote access${COLOR_RESET}"
    printf '  ssh tunnel   ssh -L 8700:localhost:8700 %s@%s\n' "${USER:-user}" "$host_label"
    printf '  then open    %s\n' "$DASHBOARD_URL"
    printf '\n'
  fi
}

resolve_launch_dir() {
  local current_dir fallback_dir
  current_dir="$(pwd)"
  if [ -w "$current_dir" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$current_dir"
    return
  fi

  fallback_dir="${HOME:-$INSTALL_ROOT}"
  warn "Current directory is not writable. Falling back to $fallback_dir for the first run."
  printf '%s\n' "$fallback_dir"
}

print_restart_command() {
  if [ -z "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM" ]; then
    LAUNCH_PLATFORM="$(resolve_launch_platform)"
  fi
  if [ -n "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM" ]; then
    printf '  vllm-sr serve --platform %s\n' "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM"
  else
    printf '  vllm-sr serve\n'
  fi
  printf '  vllm-sr dashboard\n'
}

python_supports_vllm_sr() {
  "$1" -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 10) else 1)' \
    >/dev/null 2>&1
}

python_version_of() {
  "$1" -c 'import sys; print(".".join(map(str, sys.version_info[:3])))' 2>/dev/null || printf 'unknown\n'
}

find_python() {
  if [ -n "$PYTHON_BIN" ]; then
    if ! has_cmd "$PYTHON_BIN"; then
      die "Requested Python interpreter not found: $PYTHON_BIN"
    fi
    if ! python_supports_vllm_sr "$PYTHON_BIN"; then
      die "Requested Python interpreter must be Python 3.10 or newer: $PYTHON_BIN"
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$PYTHON_BIN"
    return
  fi

  for candidate in python3 python3.12 python3.11 python3.10 python; do
    if has_cmd "$candidate" && python_supports_vllm_sr "$candidate"; then
      printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
      return
    fi
  done

  return 1
}

detect_python_candidate() {
  find_python
}

detect_linux_pkg_manager() {
  for candidate in apt-get dnf yum; do
    if has_cmd "$candidate"; then
      printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
      return
    fi
  done

  return 1
}

detect_package_manager_label() {
  local pkg_manager
  case "$OS_NAME" in
    darwin)
      if has_cmd brew; then
        printf 'homebrew\n'
      else
        printf 'homebrew (not found)\n'
      fi
      ;;
    linux)
      pkg_manager="$(detect_linux_pkg_manager || true)"
      if [ -n "$pkg_manager" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$pkg_manager"
      else
        printf 'not detected\n'
      fi
      ;;
  esac
}

detect_existing_runtime() {
  if docker_ready; then
    printf 'docker\n'
    return
  fi

  return 1
}

describe_python_dependency_plan() {
  local python_cmd pkg_manager
  python_cmd="$1"
  if [ -n "$python_cmd" ]; then
    printf 'none (using %s)\n' "$python_cmd"
    return
  fi

  case "$OS_NAME" in
    darwin)
      printf 'python via Homebrew\n'
      ;;
    linux)
      pkg_manager="$(detect_linux_pkg_manager || true)"
      case "$pkg_manager" in
        apt-get)
          printf 'python3, python3-venv, python3-pip via apt-get\n'
          ;;
        dnf)
          printf 'python3, python3-pip via dnf\n'
          ;;
        yum)
          printf 'python3, python3-pip via yum\n'
          ;;
        *)
          printf 'python 3.10+ required (install manually)\n'
          ;;
      esac
      ;;
  esac
}

describe_runtime_dependency_plan() {
  local runtime_cmd preferred_runtime pkg_manager
  runtime_cmd="$1"

  if [ "$MODE" = "cli" ] || [ "$REQUESTED_RUNTIME" = "skip" ]; then
    printf 'none\n'
    return
  fi

  if [ -n "$runtime_cmd" ]; then
    printf 'none (using existing %s)\n' "$runtime_cmd"
    return
  fi

  preferred_runtime="$(choose_runtime_preference)"
  case "$OS_NAME:$preferred_runtime" in
    darwin:docker)
      printf 'docker, colima via Homebrew\n'
      ;;
    linux:docker)
      pkg_manager="$(detect_linux_pkg_manager || true)"
      case "$pkg_manager" in
        apt-get)
          printf 'docker.io via apt-get\n'
          ;;
        dnf)
          printf 'docker via dnf\n'
          ;;
        yum)
          printf 'docker via yum\n'
          ;;
        *)
          printf 'docker required (install manually)\n'
          ;;
      esac
      ;;
    *)
      printf 'none\n'
      ;;
  esac
}

ensure_homebrew() {
  if ! has_cmd brew; then
    die "Homebrew is required on macOS when Python or a container runtime must be installed automatically."
  fi
}

install_python() {
  step "Installing Python 3.10+"

  case "$OS_NAME" in
    darwin)
      ensure_homebrew
      brew install python
      ;;
    linux)
      local pkg_manager
      pkg_manager="$(detect_linux_pkg_manager)" || die \
        "No supported Linux package manager found. Install Python 3.10+ manually and re-run the installer."
      case "$pkg_manager" in
        apt-get)
          run_as_root apt-get update
          run_as_root apt-get install -y python3 python3-venv python3-pip
          ;;
        dnf)
          run_as_root dnf install -y python3 python3-pip
          ;;
        yum)
          run_as_root yum install -y python3 python3-pip
          ;;
      esac
      ;;
  esac

  done_step "Python 3.10+ is ready"
}

create_launcher() {
  local launcher_path executable_path
  launcher_path="$BIN_DIR/vllm-sr"
  executable_path="$INSTALL_ROOT/venv/bin/vllm-sr"

  mkdir -p "$BIN_DIR"
  cat >"$launcher_path" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

exec "$executable_path" "\$@"
EOF
  chmod +x "$launcher_path"
}

install_requested_package() {
  if [ -n "$PIP_SPEC" ]; then
    run_quiet_step \
      "Installing vLLM Semantic Router from $PIP_SPEC" \
      "$INSTALL_ROOT/venv/bin/python" -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --upgrade --quiet "$PIP_SPEC"
    return
  fi

  case "$REQUESTED_CHANNEL" in
    dev)
      run_quiet_step \
        "Installing latest development vLLM Semantic Router release" \
        "$INSTALL_ROOT/venv/bin/python" -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --upgrade --quiet --pre vllm-sr
      ;;
    stable)
      run_quiet_step \
        "Installing latest stable vLLM Semantic Router release" \
        "$INSTALL_ROOT/venv/bin/python" -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --upgrade --quiet vllm-sr
      ;;
  esac
}

install_cli() {
  local python_cmd
  python_cmd="$(find_python)" || {
    info "Python 3.10+ was not found. The installer will add it now."
    install_python
    python_cmd="$(find_python)" || die "Unable to locate a Python 3.10+ interpreter after installation."
  }

  done_step "Using Python interpreter: $python_cmd"
  mkdir -p "$INSTALL_ROOT"
  step "Creating isolated environment at $INSTALL_ROOT/venv"
  "$python_cmd" -m venv "$INSTALL_ROOT/venv"
  done_step "Created isolated environment"
  run_quiet_step \
    "Bootstrapping installer Python tooling" \
    "$INSTALL_ROOT/venv/bin/python" -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --upgrade --quiet pip setuptools wheel
  install_requested_package
  step "Writing launcher to $BIN_DIR/vllm-sr"
  create_launcher
  done_step "Launcher is ready"

  local version_output
  version_output="$("$BIN_DIR/vllm-sr" --version 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -n "$version_output" ]; then
    done_step "Installed $version_output"
  else
    done_step "Installed vllm-sr"
  fi

  step "Setting up shell completions"
  if "$BIN_DIR/vllm-sr" completion install >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    done_step "Shell completions installed"
  else
    info "Shell completion auto-install skipped (run 'vllm-sr completion install' manually)"
  fi
}

docker_ready() {
  has_cmd docker && docker info >/dev/null 2>&1
}

choose_runtime_preference() {
  if [ "$REQUESTED_RUNTIME" != "auto" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$REQUESTED_RUNTIME"
    return
  fi

  case "$OS_NAME" in
    darwin)
      printf 'docker\n'
      ;;
    linux)
      printf 'docker\n'
      ;;
  esac
}

install_macos_docker_runtime() {
  ensure_homebrew
  step "Installing Docker CLI and Colima via Homebrew"
  brew install docker colima
  step "Starting Colima"
  colima start
  done_step "Docker + Colima runtime is ready"
}

install_linux_docker_runtime() {
  local pkg_manager
  pkg_manager="$(detect_linux_pkg_manager)" || die \
    "No supported Linux package manager found. Install Docker manually and re-run the installer."

  step "Installing Docker"
  case "$pkg_manager" in
    apt-get)
      run_as_root apt-get update
      run_as_root apt-get install -y docker.io
      ;;
    dnf)
      run_as_root dnf install -y docker
      ;;
    yum)
      run_as_root yum install -y docker
      ;;
  esac

  if has_cmd systemctl; then
    run_as_root systemctl enable --now docker || true
  fi

  if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    run_as_root usermod -aG docker "$USER" || true
  fi

  done_step "Docker runtime is ready"
}

write_runtime_env() {
  rm -f "$INSTALL_ROOT/runtime.env"
}

ensure_runtime() {
  if [ "$MODE" = "cli" ] || [ "$REQUESTED_RUNTIME" = "skip" ]; then
    SELECTED_RUNTIME=""
    write_runtime_env
    info "Runtime bootstrap skipped."
    return
  fi

  if docker_ready; then
    SELECTED_RUNTIME="docker"
    write_runtime_env
    done_step "Using existing Docker runtime"
    return
  fi

  case "$(choose_runtime_preference)" in
    docker)
      case "$OS_NAME" in
        darwin)
          install_macos_docker_runtime
          docker_ready || die "Docker is installed but not reachable. Try running 'colima start' and then 'vllm-sr serve'."
          SELECTED_RUNTIME="docker"
          ;;
        linux)
          install_linux_docker_runtime
          if docker_ready; then
            SELECTED_RUNTIME="docker"
          else
            die "Docker was installed but is not reachable from the current shell. Open a new shell or run 'newgrp docker', then start with 'vllm-sr serve'."
          fi
          ;;
      esac
      ;;
    *)
      die "Unsupported runtime selection: $(choose_runtime_preference)"
      ;;
  esac

  write_runtime_env
}

launch_first_session() {
  local launch_dir serve_log_file
  if ! should_auto_launch; then
    return
  fi

  LAUNCH_PLATFORM="$(resolve_launch_platform)"
  launch_dir="$(resolve_launch_dir)"

  if [ -n "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM" ]; then
    info "First-run serve command: vllm-sr serve --platform $LAUNCH_PLATFORM"
  else
    info "First-run serve command: vllm-sr serve"
  fi
  info "First-run dashboard command: vllm-sr dashboard"
  info "Starting the first local session. This can take a few minutes on the first image pull."

  step "Running first-time serve flow"
  serve_log_file="$(make_temp_log)"
  if (
    cd "$launch_dir"
    if [ -n "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM" ]; then
      "$BIN_DIR/vllm-sr" serve --platform "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM"
    else
      "$BIN_DIR/vllm-sr" serve
    fi
  ) >"$serve_log_file" 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$serve_log_file"
    AUTO_LAUNCH_RAN="1"
    done_step "First-time serve flow completed"
  else
    warn "Automatic first run did not complete. Command output follows:"
    cat "$serve_log_file" >&2
    rm -f "$serve_log_file"
    warn "Automatic first run did not complete. Retry with:"
    print_restart_command
    die "Installation finished, but the first vllm-sr serve run failed"
  fi

  step "Checking dashboard availability"
  if "$BIN_DIR/vllm-sr" dashboard --no-open >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    done_step "Dashboard is available"
  else
    warn "The dashboard command could not confirm a running session."
    print_dashboard_access
    die "Installation finished, but the dashboard did not come up cleanly"
  fi

  step "Opening dashboard"
  if open_dashboard_url; then
    done_step "Dashboard opened in your browser"
  else
    warn "Could not open a browser automatically."
    done_step "Dashboard is running"
    print_dashboard_access
  fi
}

print_path_hint() {
  local shell_path_placeholder
  shell_path_placeholder="$(printf '%s' "\$PATH")"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$BIN_DIR:"*)
      return 1
      ;;
    *)
      warn "$BIN_DIR is not on PATH."
      printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_WHITE}Current shell${COLOR_RESET}"
      printf '  export PATH="%s:%s"\n' "$BIN_DIR" "$shell_path_placeholder"
      printf '\n'
      return 0
      ;;
  esac
}

print_next_steps() {
  local primary_ip host_label

  printf '\n'
  done_step "vLLM Semantic Router is ready"

  if [ -z "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM" ]; then
    LAUNCH_PLATFORM="$(resolve_launch_platform)"
  fi

  if print_path_hint; then
    info "Add the PATH export above before running vllm-sr."
  fi

  printf '%b\n' "${COLOR_WHITE}Ready${COLOR_RESET}"
  if [ "$MODE" = "serve" ]; then
    printf '  runtime      %s\n' "${SELECTED_RUNTIME:-not configured}"
  fi

  if [ "$AUTO_LAUNCH_RAN" = "1" ]; then
    primary_ip="$(detect_primary_ip || true)"
    printf '  dashboard    %s\n' "$DASHBOARD_URL"
    if [ -n "$primary_ip" ]; then
      printf '  network      http://%s:8700\n' "$primary_ip"
    fi
    printf '  stop         vllm-sr stop\n'
    if [ -n "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM" ]; then
      printf '  restart      vllm-sr serve --platform %s\n' "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM"
    else
      printf '  restart      vllm-sr serve\n'
    fi
    if is_remote_session; then
      host_label="$(detect_host_label)"
      printf '  tunnel       ssh -L 8700:localhost:8700 %s@%s\n' "${USER:-user}" "$host_label"
    fi
  else
    printf '  verify       vllm-sr --version\n'
    if [ "$MODE" = "serve" ]; then
      if [ -n "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM" ]; then
        printf '  start        vllm-sr serve --platform %s\n' "$LAUNCH_PLATFORM"
      else
        printf '  start        vllm-sr serve\n'
      fi
      printf '  open         vllm-sr dashboard\n'
    fi
  fi
  printf '\n'
}

parse_args() {
  while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --mode)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --mode"
        MODE="$2"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --runtime)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --runtime"
        REQUESTED_RUNTIME="$2"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --install-root)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --install-root"
        INSTALL_ROOT="$2"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --bin-dir)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --bin-dir"
        BIN_DIR="$2"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --pip-spec)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --pip-spec"
        PIP_SPEC="$2"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --channel)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --channel"
        REQUESTED_CHANNEL="$2"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --python)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --python"
        PYTHON_BIN="$2"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --platform)
        [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "Missing value for --platform"
        REQUESTED_PLATFORM="$2"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --no-launch)
        AUTO_LAUNCH="0"
        shift
        ;;
      -h|--help)
        usage
        exit 0
        ;;
      *)
        die "Unknown argument: $1"
        ;;
    esac
  done
}

validate_args() {
  case "$MODE" in
    cli|serve)
      ;;
    *)
      die "--mode must be 'cli' or 'serve'"
      ;;
  esac

  case "$REQUESTED_RUNTIME" in
    auto|docker|skip)
      ;;
    *)
      die "--runtime must be one of: auto, docker, skip"
      ;;
  esac

  case "$REQUESTED_CHANNEL" in
    stable|dev)
      ;;
    *)
      die "--channel must be one of: stable, dev"
      ;;
  esac

  if ! is_truthy "$AUTO_LAUNCH" && ! is_falsey "$AUTO_LAUNCH"; then
    die "VLLM_SR_INSTALL_AUTO_LAUNCH must be a boolean-like value (1/0, true/false, yes/no)"
  fi
}

main() {
  parse_args "$@"
  validate_args
  detect_os
  print_logo
  print_install_plan
  install_cli
  ensure_runtime
  launch_first_session
  print_next_steps
}

main "$@"

4

15	  `make agent-serve-local ENV=cpu AGENT_STACK_NAME=lane-a AGENT_PORT_OFFSET=0`
16	  and `make agent-serve-local ENV=cpu AGENT_STACK_NAME=lane-b AGENT_PORT_OFFSET=200`
17	- Use the same `AGENT_STACK_NAME` and `AGENT_PORT_OFFSET` values with `make agent-smoke-local` and `make agent-stop-local`

30	- For real AMD model deployment and backend container setup, read [website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md](../../../website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md)

# Environments

## `cpu-local`

- Build with `make vllm-sr-dev`
- Local runtime defaults to the split router/envoy/dashboard topology
- Split local runtime uses the local `vllm-sr` router image directly by default
- Split Intelligent Routing for Mixture-of-Models uses the local `vllm-sr` router image directly by default
- Only if that local router image is already up to date, you can reuse it with `make vllm-sr-dev SKIP_ROUTER_IMAGE=1`
- Start with `vllm-sr serve --image-pull-policy never`
- Use this for the default local Docker workflow
- Default smoke config: [config.agent-smoke.cpu.yaml](../../../e2e/config/config.agent-smoke.cpu.yaml)
- If you need a non-default config, run `make agent-serve-local ENV=cpu AGENT_SERVE_CONFIG=<config>`
- For isolated parallel local stacks, add `AGENT_STACK_NAME=<name>` and `AGENT_PORT_OFFSET=<n>`, for example:
  `make agent-serve-local ENV=cpu AGENT_STACK_NAME=lane-a AGENT_PORT_OFFSET=0`
  and `make agent-serve-local ENV=cpu AGENT_STACK_NAME=lane-b AGENT_PORT_OFFSET=200`
- Use the same `AGENT_STACK_NAME` and `AGENT_PORT_OFFSET` values with `make agent-smoke-local` and `make agent-stop-local`

## `amd-local`

- Build with `make vllm-sr-dev VLLM_SR_PLATFORM=amd`
- Local runtime defaults to the split router/envoy/dashboard topology
- Split local runtime uses the local `vllm-sr-rocm` router image directly by default
- Only if that local router image is already up to date, you can reuse it with `make vllm-sr-dev VLLM_SR_PLATFORM=amd SKIP_ROUTER_IMAGE=1`
- Start with `vllm-sr serve --image-pull-policy never --platform amd`
- Use this for ROCm/AMD validation and platform-default image checks
- Default smoke config: [config.agent-smoke.amd.yaml](../../../e2e/config/config.agent-smoke.amd.yaml)
- If you need a non-default config, run `make agent-serve-local ENV=amd AGENT_SERVE_CONFIG=<config>`
- The same `AGENT_STACK_NAME=<name>` and `AGENT_PORT_OFFSET=<n>` overrides work for isolated AMD-local stacks
- For real AMD model deployment and backend container setup, read [website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md](../../../website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md)
- Use [config/recipes/balance/config.yaml](../../../config/recipes/balance/config.yaml) as the reference YAML-first AMD routing profile
- See [amd-local.md](amd-local.md)

## `nvidia-local`

- Build with `VLLM_SR_PLATFORM=nvidia make vllm-sr-build`
- Local runtime uses the `ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-cuda:latest` image (published via `docker-publish.yml` / `docker-release.yml`); a local build tagged `vllm-sr-cuda:local` is also supported
- Start with `vllm-sr serve --platform nvidia --config <recipe>` — `--platform nvidia` selects the published CUDA image, wires `--gpus all` / CDI passthrough, and flips `use_cpu` to false for router internal models under `global.model_catalog`, at parity with `--platform amd`. Pass `--image` / `VLLM_SR_IMAGE` only to pin a specific image, and `VLLM_SR_NVIDIA_PRESERVE_CPU=1` to keep the recipe's CPU settings
- Use this for CUDA/NVIDIA validation of BERT classifiers, mmBERT embeddings, jailbreak guard, PII detection, and other router-side ML modules on GPU
- Verified hardware in the playbook: RTX 4090 (compute_cap 8.9), CUDA driver 580
- Set `use_cpu: false` under `global.model_catalog` in your routing recipe for the modules you want on GPU
- For the full router-on-CUDA build/serve/validation playbook, read [nvidia-local.md](nvidia-local.md)
- Note: `deploy/nvidia/` is intentionally empty until an NVIDIA-specific routing profile (a real backend recipe parallel to [website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md](../../../website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md)) is authored — that is separate work from this router-on-GPU environment

## `ci-k8s`

- Run local profile checks with `make e2e-test E2E_PROFILE=<profile>`
- CI expands to the standard kind/Kubernetes matrix in [integration-test-k8s.yml](../../../.github/workflows/integration-test-k8s.yml)

## Selection Rule

- Default to `cpu-local`
- Use `amd-local` when platform behavior, ROCm image selection, or AMD defaults are affected
- Use `nvidia-local` when CUDA image selection, NVIDIA GPU passthrough, or router-side ML modules on GPU are affected
- Use `ci-k8s` for merge-gate coverage and all profile-sensitive routing/deploy behavior

1	# vLLM Semantic Router on NVIDIA CUDA
2	
3	This playbook documents how to run the **router itself** (BERT
4	classifiers + embedding-driven KB lookup) on an NVIDIA GPU. Scope is
5	router-side ML inference — BERT-based intent classification, PII
6	detection, jailbreak guard, mmBERT embedding for Knowledge-Base
7	signals, hallucination mitigation, feedback detection. The backend
8	LLM is reached over the network and is **not** served from this host.
9	
10	**How this relates to `amd-local.md`:** this file is the NVIDIA
11	equivalent of [`amd-local.md`](amd-local.md) — how to build the router
12	image on CUDA and serve it with `vllm-sr serve --platform nvidia`.
13	Both live under `tools/agent/docs/` and have matching entries in
14	[`environments.md`](environments.md).
15	
16	[`website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md`](../../../website/docs/installation/amd-rocm.md) is a different
17	concern: a *routing profile* guide (the `balance.yaml` recipe running
18	against a single ROCm vLLM backend). The naming looks parallel but
19	the topic isn't. `deploy/nvidia/` is intentionally left empty until a
20	matching NVIDIA routing profile is authored.
21	
22	> **When this playbook is NOT for you:** upstream `onnx-binding/README.md`
23	> documents CPU≈GPU latency parity for BERT-size embeddings at small
24	> batches. If your only goal is "make the router faster", measure CPU
25	> latency first — you may not need GPU at all. Use this playbook when
26	> you specifically need GPU residency (very large batches, very high
27	> classifier QPS, or co-location with other GPU tenants on the same
28	> host).
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Overview
33	
34	- Runtime image: `ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-cuda:latest`
35	  (published to `ghcr.io` via `docker-publish.yml` on `main` / nightly and
36	  `docker-release.yml` on tag releases; local build still supported —
37	  see Step 1)
38	- Dockerfile: [`src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda`](../../../src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda)
39	- Inference backend: **ONNX Runtime + CUDA Execution Provider**
40	  (mirrors how ROCm path uses ORT + ROCm EP — `candle-binding` import is
41	  rewritten to `onnx-binding` at module level via `go.onnx.mod`)
42	- Config overrides: added under `global.model_catalog` in your routing
43	  recipe (see Step 2)
44	- Verified hardware: RTX 4090 (compute_cap 8.9), CUDA driver 580
45	- Verified BERT-family modules on GPU:
46	  - `embeddings.semantic` (mmBERT 32k 2D-Matryoshka)
47	  - `prompt_guard` (jailbreak detector)
48	  - `classifier.domain` (intent classifier)
49	  - `classifier.pii` (PII detector)
50	  - `hallucination_mitigation.{fact_check, detector, explainer}`
51	  - `feedback_detector`
52	
53	### Required runtime fix (must be in the image)
54	
55	Building the CUDA image and setting `use_cpu: false` is **not sufficient**
56	on its own. The classifier execution-provider selection in onnx-binding
57	had a defect where the `Auto` provider only attempted ROCm, never CUDA,
58	so on a CUDA build every classifier (intent, PII, jailbreak, factcheck)
59	silently fell back to CPU. The embedding path also created unbounded CUDA
60	arenas that OOM'd later sessions. Both are fixed in:
61	
62	- `onnx-binding/src/model_architectures/classification/mmbert_classifier.rs`
63	  — `Auto` arm now tries CUDA when the `cuda` feature is built.
64	- `onnx-binding/src/model_architectures/embedding/mmbert_embedding.rs`
65	  — CUDA sessions now use `with_memory_limit` + `SameAsRequested` arena
66	  strategy, matching the classifier path.
67	
68	If you build the image from a tree that predates these fixes, the image
69	will run, attach the GPU, and still execute classifiers on CPU. Verify
70	with Step 4b below (you must see multiple `Using CUDA execution provider`
71	lines, not just one for embedding).
72	
73	---
74	
75	## Prerequisites
76	
77	On the host:
78	
79	1. NVIDIA driver supporting CUDA 12.x runtime (verified: driver 580 with
80	   CUDA 13.0 host runtime; backward-compatible with the CUDA 12.4
81	   container runtime used in the image).
82	2. `nvidia-container-toolkit` installed and configured for Docker so
83	   `--gpus all` and `--runtime nvidia` resolve.
84	3. Verify the host can see a GPU before continuing:
85	
86	   ```bash
87	   nvidia-smi
88	   docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi
89	   ```
90	
91	   Both must list the same GPU. If the second fails, fix
92	   nvidia-container-toolkit before going further.
93	
94	4. **A running `vllm-sr` deployment** (started via `vllm-sr serve` or
95	   your own orchestration). This playbook only swaps the router
96	   container; everything else (envoy, backend, dependencies) is left
97	   untouched. See the top-level project README for the standard
98	   `vllm-sr serve` bootstrap if you do not already have one running.
99	
100	---
101	
102	## Step 1: Pull or build the CUDA image
103	
104	### 1a. Pull the published image (recommended)
105	
106	`vllm-sr-cuda` is published to `ghcr.io` on every merge to `main`,
107	nightly, and each tag release (via
108	[`docker-publish.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml) and
109	[`docker-release.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/docker-release.yml)):
110	
111	```bash
112	docker pull ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-cuda:latest
113	```
114	
115	Substitute the immutable tag (e.g. `v0.3.0`) for `latest` in production.
116	
117	Available tags on `ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-cuda`:
118	
119	- `latest` — most recent `main`
120	- `nightly-<YYYYMMDD>` — nightly build from a specific date
121	- `v<X>.<Y>.<Z>` — immutable release tag
122	
123	### 1b. Build locally (advanced / dev)
124	
125	Local build is only needed to iterate on `Dockerfile.cuda` itself or to
126	build a tree that predates the published image. The image is
127	multi-stage: it cross-builds `candle-binding`, `ml-binding`,
128	`nlp-binding` (CPU-only by design), then builds `onnx-binding` with
129	`--features "cuda,ort/load-dynamic"`, then assembles a runtime stage on
130	top of `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu22.04` with
131	`onnxruntime-gpu==1.22.0`.
132	
133	Recommended path — the Make target (wires `Dockerfile.cuda` +
134	`linux/amd64` + `vllm-sr-cuda` image name automatically):
135	
136	```bash
137	cd /path/to/semantic-router
138	VLLM_SR_PLATFORM=nvidia make vllm-sr-build
139	```
140	
141	The `VLLM_SR_PLATFORM=nvidia` block in
142	[`tools/make/docker.mk`](../../../tools/make/docker.mk) resolves the router
143	image to `vllm-sr-cuda`, dockerfile to `src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda`,
144	and arch to `amd64`.
145	
146	Equivalent raw `docker build` (if you cannot use `make`):
147	
148	```bash
149	cd /path/to/semantic-router
150	
151	DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build \
152	    --platform linux/amd64 \
153	    --build-arg TARGETARCH=amd64 \
154	    --build-arg BUILDPLATFORM=linux/amd64 \
155	    -f src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda \
156	    -t vllm-sr-cuda:local \
157	    .
158	```
159	
160	Expected build time: **~20 minutes cold**, ~3 minutes warm. Expected
161	image size: **~4.2 GB** (vs ~440 MB for the default CPU image).
162	
163	A per-Dockerfile ignore file
164	([`Dockerfile.cuda.dockerignore`](../../../src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda.dockerignore))
165	excludes runtime-state directories (`.vllm-sr/`, `milvus-data/`,
166	`etcd/`, `postgres-data/`) so the build context loader does not hit
167	EACCES on root-owned subdirectories.
168	
169	### Verify the image before swapping containers
170	
171	The remaining steps in this playbook use the shell variable
172	`$VLLM_SR_CUDA_IMAGE` to refer to whichever image you picked in 1a or
173	1b — set it once here:
174	
175	```bash
176	# Pulled path (1a):
177	export VLLM_SR_CUDA_IMAGE=ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-cuda:latest
178	
179	# Locally built path (1b):
180	# export VLLM_SR_CUDA_IMAGE=vllm-sr-cuda:local
181	```
182	
183	```bash
184	# ORT inside the image must list CUDAExecutionProvider:
185	docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /opt/vllm-sr-venv/bin/python \
186	    "$VLLM_SR_CUDA_IMAGE" -c '
187	import onnxruntime as ort
188	print("ORT version:", ort.__version__)
189	print("Providers:", ort.get_available_providers())
190	assert "CUDAExecutionProvider" in ort.get_available_providers()
191	print("OK")
192	'
193	```
194	
195	Expected:
196	
197	```
198	ORT version: 1.22.0
199	Providers: ['TensorrtExecutionProvider', 'CUDAExecutionProvider', 'CPUExecutionProvider']
200	OK
201	```
202	
203	If `CUDAExecutionProvider` is absent, do **not** continue. Re-check
204	that `--gpus all` works on the host and the build did not silently
205	fall back to the CPU wheel.
206	
207	---
208	
209	## Step 2: Apply the config override
210	
211	The router defaults every BERT/embedding module to `use_cpu: true`
212	(see [`canonical_defaults.go`](../../../src/semantic-router/pkg/config/canonical_defaults.go)).
213	Without overrides, even when the container has GPU access, the router
214	runs entirely on CPU.
215	
216	Add the following override block under `global.model_catalog` in your
217	routing recipe (e.g. [`config/recipes/balance/config.yaml`](../../../config/recipes/balance/config.yaml)
218	or whichever recipe your deployment loads):
219	
220	```yaml
221	global:
222	  router:
223	    config_source: file
224	    strategy: priority
225	  model_catalog:
226	    embeddings:
227	      semantic:
228	        use_cpu: false
229	    modules:
230	      prompt_guard:
231	        use_cpu: false
232	      classifier:
233	        domain:
234	          use_cpu: false
235	        pii:
236	          use_cpu: false
237	      hallucination_mitigation:
238	        fact_check:
239	          use_cpu: false
240	        detector:
241	          use_cpu: false
242	        explainer:
243	          use_cpu: false
244	      feedback_detector:
245	        use_cpu: false
246	```
247	
248	This block is a **no-op on CPU images** — ORT only exposes
249	`CPUExecutionProvider` there, so `use_cpu: false` simply has no GPU EP
250	to fall back to and the module stays on CPU. Safe to leave committed.
251	
252	Note that `vllm-sr serve` reads the **transformed** runtime config
253	(`runtime-config.yaml`), not the source recipe directly. If your
254	tooling snapshots the recipe into a runtime config, make sure the
255	override flows all the way through to the runtime config the router
256	actually loads.
257	
258	---
259	
260	## Step 3: Start the router on the CUDA image
261	
262	### Recommended: `vllm-sr serve --platform nvidia`
263	
264	`vllm-sr serve --platform nvidia` now does everything this step used to
265	require by hand:
266	
267	1. selects the published CUDA image
268	   (`ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-cuda:latest`) — the
269	   same default the AMD path uses for ROCm,
270	2. attaches the GPU (`--gpus all` on Docker, CDI
271	   `nvidia.com/gpu=all` on Podman), and
272	3. flips `use_cpu` to `false` for the router internal models under
273	   `global.model_catalog`, so the Step 2 override block is applied
274	   automatically even if your recipe still defaults to CPU.
275	
276	```bash
277	vllm-sr serve --platform nvidia --config <your-recipe>.yaml
278	```
279	
280	Overrides, if you need them:
281	
282	- `--image <ref>` or `VLLM_SR_IMAGE=<ref>` — pin a specific CUDA image
283	  (bypasses the default). `VLLM_SR_IMAGE_NVIDIA` sets the nvidia-only
284	  default without affecting other platforms.
285	- `VLLM_SR_NVIDIA_PRESERVE_CPU=1` — keep the recipe's `use_cpu` values
286	  instead of flipping them to `false` (use when the router shares a GPU
287	  that has no spare headroom).
288	- `VLLM_SR_NVIDIA_GPU_PASSTHROUGH=0` — skip `--gpus all` injection.
289	
290	If steps 4a–4e below pass, you are done — skip the manual recipe.
291	
292	### Fallback: manual `docker run` (older `vllm-sr`, or custom orchestration)
293	
294	Use this only on a `vllm-sr` build that predates `--platform nvidia`
295	image selection, or when you drive the container yourself. `vllm-sr
296	serve` calls `docker run` internally with a fixed set of mounts, env
297	vars, ports, and network; to run the CUDA image by hand, recreate the
298	container with the same spec **plus** `--gpus all`.
299	
300	### 3a. Capture the running container spec
301	
302	```bash
303	# Save current container's env vars to a 600-mode file (may contain API keys)
304	docker inspect vllm-sr-router-container --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{.}}
305	{{end}}' | \
306	    grep -E '^(ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|OPENAI_API_KEY|SR_LOG_LEVEL|OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT|VLLM_SR_DASHBOARD_CONTAINER_NAME|VLLM_SR_ENVOY_CONTAINER_NAME|VLLM_SR_ROUTER_CONTAINER_NAME|VLLM_SR_RUNTIME_CONFIG_PATH|VLLM_SR_SOURCE_CONFIG_PATH)=' \
307	    > /tmp/router-env.list
308	chmod 600 /tmp/router-env.list
309	```
310	
311	> Adjust the env-var allowlist to match whatever your deployment
312	> actually sets (backend API keys, telemetry endpoints, container
313	> names, config paths).
314	>
315	> Do **not** copy `PATH`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, or `VIRTUAL_ENV` from the
316	> old container — the new image sets its own values (different paths
317	> for CUDA runtime libs). Pulling them across will break ORT's dynamic
318	> loader.
319	
320	### 3b. Stop and remove the old container
321	
322	```bash
323	docker stop vllm-sr-router-container
324	docker rm vllm-sr-router-container
325	```
326	
327	### 3c. Start the new container with `--gpus all`
328	
329	```bash
330	docker run -d \
331	    --name vllm-sr-router-container \
332	    --network vllm-sr-network \
333	    --gpus all \
334	    --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
335	    -p 0.0.0.0:50051:50051 \
336	    -p 0.0.0.0:8080:8080 \
337	    -p 0.0.0.0:9190:9190 \
338	    --env-file /tmp/router-env.list \
339	    -v "$(pwd)/models:/app/models" \
340	    -v "$(pwd)/active-config.yaml:/app/config.yaml" \
341	    -v "$(pwd)/.vllm-sr:/app/.vllm-sr" \
342	    -w /app \
343	    "$VLLM_SR_CUDA_IMAGE" \
344	    /app/.vllm-sr/runtime-config.yaml /app/.vllm-sr
345	```
346	
347	Adjust the host paths, ports, and network name to match your
348	deployment's layout.
349	
350	---
351	
352	## Step 4: Verify the router is on GPU
353	
354	Wait ~30 seconds for model load, then run the checks below in order.
355	
356	### 4a. Container is alive and not crash-looping
357	
358	```bash
359	docker ps --filter "name=vllm-sr-router-container" --format \
360	    "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Image}}"
361	```
362	
363	Expected: `Up <N> seconds`, image matches `$VLLM_SR_CUDA_IMAGE` from
364	Step 1 (either
365	`ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-cuda:latest` or
366	`vllm-sr-cuda:local`).
367	
368	### 4b. Router actually selected the CUDA EP
369	
370	```bash
371	docker logs vllm-sr-router-container 2>&1 | \
372	    grep "Using CUDA execution provider"
373	```
374	
375	Expected (one line per loaded ONNX model):
376	
377	```
378	INFO: Using CUDA execution provider (NVIDIA GPU) — verified
379	INFO: Using CUDA execution provider (NVIDIA GPU) — verified
380	...
381	```
382	
383	If you see `Using CPU execution provider` everywhere, work through these
384	causes in order:
385	
386	1. **Config override not applied** — re-check that `runtime-config.yaml`
387	   (not just the source recipe) contains the `model_catalog` block;
388	   the router reads `runtime-config.yaml`.
389	2. **Image predates the EP fix** — see "Required runtime fix" in the
390	   Overview. Without it, embedding loads on CUDA but every classifier
391	   stays on CPU regardless of config.
392	3. **Out of VRAM** — see "Some models load on CUDA, others fall back to
393	   CPU" in Troubleshooting; check `nvidia-smi` free memory.
394	
395	### 4c. GPU memory actually allocated to BERT weights
396	
397	```bash
398	nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv
399	```
400	
401	Compared with a CPU-only baseline you should see **~3 GB additional
402	memory used** (BERT mmBERT + classifier models resident on device).
403	Concrete observed delta on RTX 4090: `17986 MiB → 21139 MiB`
404	(+3153 MiB).
405	
406	### 4d. `embedding_models_init_started` shows `use_cpu: false`
407	
408	```bash
409	docker logs vllm-sr-router-container 2>&1 | \
410	    grep embedding_models_init_started | tail -1 | python3 -m json.tool
411	```
412	
413	Expected: `"use_cpu": false`.
414	
415	### 4e. KB classifier is operational
416	
417	```bash
418	docker logs vllm-sr-router-container 2>&1 | \
419	    grep knowledge_base_classifier_initialized
420	```
421	
422	Expected: one `knowledge_base_classifier_initialized` line per KB in
423	the active config.
424	
425	---
426	
427	## Step 5: Sanity-check a real query
428	
429	Send any prompt through the router and confirm it routes successfully:
430	
431	```bash
432	curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8899/v1/chat/completions \
433	    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
434	    -d '{
435	      "model": "auto",
436	      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the LEED standard?"}]
437	    }' | head
438	```
439	
440	The router applies its decision tree (n-gram → KB embedding similarity
441	→ decision rule), routes to the appropriate backend, and the response
442	flows back through envoy. If steps 4a-4e all pass and a real query
443	returns 200, you are done.
444	
445	---
446	
447	## Rollback
448	
449	If the CUDA image misbehaves, rollback is one container restart on the
450	default CPU image:
451	
452	```bash
453	docker stop vllm-sr-router-container
454	docker rm vllm-sr-router-container
455	# bring the router back up on the default CPU image via your normal
456	# `vllm-sr serve` flow
457	```
458	
459	The `model_catalog` overrides remain in the recipe but are silently
460	ignored on the CPU image, so no further config change is needed.
461	
462	---
463	
464	## Troubleshooting
465	
466	### `huggingface-cli not found` at router startup
467	
468	Symptom: container exits with code 1, log ends with:
469	
470	```
471	huggingface-cli check failed: huggingface-cli not found
472	```
473	
474	Cause: `huggingface_hub==1.5.0` ships the `hf` CLI but does not pull
475	`click` as a hard dependency under Python 3.10. The runtime image is
476	Ubuntu 22.04 + Python 3.10.
477	
478	Fix: this is already addressed in
479	[`Dockerfile.cuda`](../../../src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda) (the pip
480	install line includes `'click>=8.1.7'`). If you see this on a stale local
481	build, rebuild the image.
482	
483	### `Error: mmBERT model not initialized` in the log
484	
485	Some initial errors during the **first second** of startup are normal —
486	the KB classifier tries to embed exemplars before the model finishes
487	loading and retries them once it does. They should stop within the
488	first 1-2 seconds. If errors continue indefinitely, the model never
489	loaded; check:
490	
491	```bash
492	docker logs vllm-sr-router-container 2>&1 | \
493	    grep -iE "Selected mmBERT ONNX|Loading layer|Using.*execution provider"
494	```
495	
496	You should see one `Selected mmBERT ONNX file: ...` and several
497	`Loading layer-N from ...` lines. If they are absent, the model files
498	are not visible inside the container — re-check the
499	`-v $(pwd)/models:/app/models` bind mount.
500	
501	### `--gpus all` rejected with "could not select device driver"
502	
503	Cause: `nvidia-container-toolkit` is not installed or not registered as
504	a Docker runtime. Reinstall and reload:
505	
506	```bash
507	sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
508	sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
509	sudo systemctl restart docker
510	```
511	
512	Verify with:
513	
514	```bash
515	docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi
516	```
517	
518	### GPU memory does not increase after restart
519	
520	Most likely cause: you edited the source recipe (the snapshot) but did
521	**not** regenerate the runtime config (`runtime-config.yaml`). The
522	router reads `runtime-config.yaml`, not the source recipe.
523	
524	Fix: either re-run your config-transform step (full regenerate) or
525	patch `runtime-config.yaml` directly for a quick test.
526	
527	### Performance still feels identical to CPU
528	
529	This is expected for small-batch BERT (the canonical mmBERT 32k
530	embedding model). Upstream
531	[`onnx-binding/README.md`](../../../onnx-binding/README.md) reports
532	CPU ≈ GPU latency at batch size 1 for sequence lengths up to 512. The
533	real win from this image is:
534	
535	- **High-QPS scenarios** (many concurrent queries hitting the embedding
536	  model at once)
537	- **Co-tenancy** (you already need GPU on the same host for vLLM and
538	  want a single hardware accelerator footprint)
539	- **Future model upgrades** (when you move to larger embedding /
540	  classifier models that GPUs accelerate proportionally more)
541	
542	For today's small mmBERT-32k workload at low QPS, the CPU image is
543	genuinely competitive. Benchmark before and after under your **actual**
544	QPS pattern before declaring victory.
545	
546	### Some models load on CUDA, others fall back to CPU (mixed state)
547	
548	Symptom: the startup log shows a mix of `Using CUDA execution provider`
549	and `Using CPU execution provider`, and may include:
550	
551	```
552	WARN: CUDA EP failed: ... bfc_arena.cc ... Failed to allocate memory ...
553	WARN: CUDA EP failed: ... CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED ...
554	```
555	
556	Cause: not enough free VRAM. The router opens several CUDA sessions
557	(one primary embedding session, one per 2D-Matryoshka early-exit layer,
558	plus one per classifier). Each session needs a cuBLAS handle and an arena
559	block. On a GPU shared with other tenants (e.g. a co-located vLLM serving
560	a large model), the later sessions OOM and silently fall back to CPU.
561	
562	Diagnose:
563	
564	```bash
565	# How much VRAM is actually free, and who is using it
566	nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv
567	nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv
568	```
569	
570	If `memory.free` is only a few hundred MB while another process holds
571	most of the card, that is the cause — not a code bug.
572	
573	Fixes, in order of preference:
574	
575	1. **Cap per-session arena size.** Set `ORT_GPU_MEM_LIMIT` to a small
576	   value (e.g. `512MB`) so every session fits into the limited free VRAM:
577	
578	   ```bash
579	   # via the container env
580	   docker run ... -e ORT_GPU_MEM_LIMIT=512MB "$VLLM_SR_CUDA_IMAGE" ...
581	   ```
582	
583	   The embedding and classifier CUDA branches both honor
584	   `get_gpu_mem_limit()`, which reads this env var first (supports
585	   `512MB`, `4GB`, or raw bytes). Without it they auto-probe free VRAM,
586	   and the auto-probe falls back to 4 GB per session when it cannot read
587	   the GPU — too large on a contended card.
588	
589	   > Note: `ORT_GPU_MEM_LIMIT` may not be in the `vllm-sr` CLI
590	   > passthrough allowlist (`runtime_support.py: PASSTHROUGH_ENV_RULES`).
591	   > To use it via `vllm-sr serve` you must either add it to that
592	   > allowlist or use the manual `docker run` path (Step 3c).
593	
594	2. **Free up VRAM** by stopping or shrinking the co-tenant process
595	   (other vLLM instance, etc.).
596	
597	3. **Accept the mixed state.** A CPU-resident classifier still works
598	   correctly; for the small mmBERT-32k models the latency difference is
599	   minor (see the section above). The bounded-arena fix degrades to CPU
600	   gracefully rather than crashing.
601	
602	To verify which model fell back, align the `Using CPU` lines with the
603	nearest preceding `*_detector_backend_loading` / `Loading layer-N` log
604	line.
605	
606	### Confirm the GPU is actually computing (not just holding weights)
607	
608	Memory being resident on the GPU proves the model loaded there, but not
609	that inference runs on it. To confirm live GPU compute, monitor the
610	router process's SM utilization while sending classification requests:
611	
612	```bash
613	# Find the router's GPU PID
614	ROUTER_PID=$(nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name --format=csv,noheader \
615	  | grep router | cut -d, -f1 | tr -d ' ')
616	
617	# Sample per-process SM% for 10s; send requests in the middle
618	nvidia-smi pmon -i 0 -c 10 -o T &
619	sleep 3
620	for i in $(seq 1 15); do
621	  curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/classify/intent \
622	    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
623	    -d '{"text":"Explain TCP vs UDP and when to use each"}'
624	done
625	```
626	
627	The router PID's `sm` column should rise from `-`/`0` (idle) to a small
628	positive value during the request burst, then return to idle. That
629	transition is the proof GPU compute happened. (The value stays low for
630	small BERT models on a fast GPU — that is expected, not a problem.)
631	
632	---
633	
634	## Router image differences: NVIDIA CUDA vs AMD ROCm
635	
636	Apples-to-apples comparison of the two GPU-enabled router images,
637	sourced from `src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda` and
638	`src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.rocm`:
639	
640	| Aspect | AMD ROCm router (`vllm-sr-rocm`) | NVIDIA CUDA router (`vllm-sr-cuda`) |
641	|---|---|---|
642	| Published tag | `ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-rocm:latest` | `ghcr.io/vllm-project/semantic-router/vllm-sr-cuda:latest` |
643	| Base image | `rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.0` | `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu22.04` |
644	| ORT wheel | `onnxruntime_rocm-1.22.1` (radeon repo) | `onnxruntime-gpu==1.22.0` (PyPI) |
645	| `onnx-binding` feature | `--features rocm-dynamic` | `--features "cuda,ort/load-dynamic"` |
646	| GPU passthrough | `--device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri` | `--gpus all` (Docker) or CDI `nvidia.com/gpu=all` (Podman) |
647	| CLI entrypoint | `vllm-sr serve --platform amd` | `vllm-sr serve --platform nvidia` (selects the CUDA image + flips `use_cpu` to false, at parity with the AMD path) |
648	
649	The two images are independent; do not mix `--gpus all` with
650	`--device=/dev/kfd` on the same router container.
651	
652	---
653	
654	## Files involved
655	
656	- [`src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda`](../../../src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda) —
657	  the runtime image, mirrored from `Dockerfile.rocm`
658	- [`src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda.dockerignore`](../../../src/vllm-sr/Dockerfile.cuda.dockerignore) —
659	  per-Dockerfile ignore, excludes runtime-state dirs
660	- [`onnx-binding/Cargo.toml`](../../../onnx-binding/Cargo.toml) — feature
661	  graph (`cuda`, `rocm`, `rocm-dynamic`, etc.); read this if you need
662	  to understand or change which EP is compiled in
663	- [`src/semantic-router/go.onnx.mod`](../../../src/semantic-router/go.onnx.mod) —
664	  the `replace` directive that rewires `candle-binding` Go imports to
665	  `onnx-binding` at module level. This is the mechanism that lets a
666	  config field named `embeddings.semantic.use_cpu` (originally a candle
667	  concept) actually steer the ONNX Runtime EP selection
668	- [`src/semantic-router/pkg/config/canonical_defaults.go`](../../../src/semantic-router/pkg/config/canonical_defaults.go) —
669	  source of truth for `use_cpu: true` defaults
670	- [`tools/make/docker.mk`](../../../tools/make/docker.mk) — the
671	  `VLLM_SR_PLATFORM=nvidia` block wiring `Dockerfile.cuda` +
672	  `vllm-sr-cuda` image name + `linux/amd64` into the Make path
673	- [`.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml) —
674	  publishes `vllm-sr-cuda` to `ghcr.io` on merge to `main` and nightly
675	  (amd64-only, matching ROCm)
676	- [`.github/workflows/docker-release.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/docker-release.yml) —
677	  publishes tagged `vllm-sr-cuda` releases on `v*` tags
